newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-Capel ups New England Elec.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Capel ups New England Elec.

text.p: HSBC James Capel has raised New England Electric System to buy from hold after it sold its generating assets to PG&E Corp for $1.59 billion, analyst Daniel Ford said in a research note.
"We are upgrading shares of NES to buy from neutral and raising our 12-month share price target to $41," Ford said.
Ford also raised New England's 1998 earnings per share forecasts to $3.24 from $3.05 and 1999 to $3.53 from $3.30.
He said that a share buyback announced by New England would add to earnings per share by $0.25.
He said that the $1.59 billion price tag exceeded estimates of $1.2 billion and the $1.1 billion book value of the 5,000 megawatts of generating assets.
Ford said he is maintaining PG&E as neutral with a $24 price target as there could be some near-term share price weakness after the price paid.
He noted that although a share buyback could provide some support, the purchase had reduced the ability to buy shares.
"PG&E's longer term startegy to be an upstream player appears to be developing rapidly, but it appears scale and scope are expensive," Ford said.
PG&E also faces a rate case review in the fourth quarter of 1997, which Ford said is expected to be widely contested.
PG&E shares were off 7/16 at 23-7/8 by 1006 EDT, New England was up 1-5/8 to 38-5/8.
